HRA Analysis: SMARTER THAN YOU (1) has been in excellent form this campaign and draws ideally in this race. He has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in the early stages which should see him very hard to run down. DOUGS FLAME (8) was very well driven last time out to nab the leaders back trail and did well there to hang on for third behind the very smart pair of Final Deadline and Fate Awaits. She should get a good run through early in this race and should be suited by the step back to 1660. BAINBRIDGE (2) starts first up in this race for the stable of Trent Dawson having previously done his racing in NSW. He is a horse with very high speed and should be suited by the soft draw in this race where he can settle close to the speed without doing too much work. MOSSDALE TERRY (9) should secure a good run off the speed in this race and has been racing well. He ran well three starts ago finishing second behind Isla Rochelle over the 2138 at this track. SELECTIONS: SMARTER THAN YOU (1), DOUGS FLAME (8), BAINBRIDGE (2), MOSSDALE TERRY (9) SUGGESTED BET: SMARTER THAN YOU (1) to win.

FIFTY THREE STARS (2) should have the gate speed to work forward and find the lead in the early stages of this race from a good draw. He drew poorly last time out and was making up good ground late to not be beaten too far by Our Rocky in a strong race. He looks hard to beat. QUIK CHANGE (1) draws ideally in this race and can lead before having options from there. In this type of grade he seems to be best when driven with a sit which should see him get every chance in this race. SPUNKYS GOTSECRETS (7) was forced to race without cover last time out over the 1660 and battled on well there to finish second behind smart Kiwi Mostart. He may be left to do the work again in this race from a wide draw but should run well again. STARZZZ DESTINY (4) was able to show good gate speed last time out to lead and run well from there for third. He should be able to press forward and race in a prominent position from a reasonable draw and should be thereabouts again. SELECTIONS: FIFTY THREE STARS (2), QUIK CHANGE (1), SPUNKYS GOTSECRETS (7), STARZZZ DESTINY (4) SUGGESTED BET: FIFTY THREE STARS (2) to win.

MOSTERT (2) didn’t have much luck on QLD debut when making a wide run into it before just being nabbed late by Beyond Doubt. He was able to then break through nicely last time out making a wide run into it to score a good win. If he can work to the lead this time he is likely to take plenty of running down. TARGARYEN (1) should be able to secure a good run behind the speed in this race from the ideal draw. He was left without cover which doesn’t usually suit him and was able to battle on nicely for third. He should be hard to hold out late. HES ALL TORQUE (8) should get a good run through behind a horse which is likely to settle close in the run. He was able to score a hat-trick of wins recently which included a win in the showcase final at Redcliffe after starting from a 40m handicap and breaking the track record. STORMTIDE (3) has really bounced back into impressive form recently scoring a good win earlier in the week when running over the top to beat Rock Hammer. He should settle close enough and looks a horse which could add value to exotics in this race. SELECTIONS: MOSTERT (2), TARGARYEN (1), HES ALL TORQUE (8), STORMTIDE (3) SUGGESTED BET: MOSTERT (2) to win.

LEAP TO FAME (7) returned in terrific style last time out when being forced to race outside of Captain Shuffles who attempted to run him off his legs first up from a spell over the 1660. It looked as though for a brief moment Captain Shuffles may have had the upper hand before Leap To Fame kicked into another gear and just cruised on by running through the line powerfully and winning with authority rating a brilliant 1.49.1 mile rate. This looks an easier assignment in this race and it appears the only question is times and margins. TIMS A TROOPER (5) was able to show enough speed to drive through and lead last time out in a race where they went a frantic tempo setting it up for DASHING (6) to run over the top late. He is likely to be driven a touch more conservatively early this time and can look to be running on late. DASHING (6) was able to return nicely from a spell last time out when getting back and being suited by a frantic tempo which allowed him to run over the top late and beat Manila Playboy. He is a horse with relatively good gate speed and from a wide draw has options in the early stages of this race. DISTRICT ATTORNEY (4) secured a good run last time out behind Captain Shuffles when battling on reasonably for fourth. If he could zip across early in this race he would have rough top three claims and reasonable top four claims. SELECTIONS: LEAP TO FAME (7), TIMS A TROOPER (5), DASHING (6), DISTRICT ATTORNEY (4) SUGGESTED BET: TIMS A TROOPER (5) to win.

NEXT TO ME (1) should have the gate speed to drive through and lead this from the ideal draw. He secured a good run last time out in a very strong race taken out by Our Rocky and wasn’t beaten too far there. He should run well. JOHN WAYNE (4) drew poorly last time out when running a good fourth at this track. He was very good winning recently over the 2040 at Redcliffe. He should be suited by the distance of this race and looks to have good each way claims. BETTOR CHEER (9) was forced to make a very wide run into it last start and was making up good ground into second. He should get a good run off the speed and can be running on late again. ROCK HAMMER (3) led last time out and may have just gone a bit too fast out in front when being run down by Stormtide after rolling along throughout. He should settle close from a low front row draw and has claims with the right run. SELECTIONS: NEXT TO ME (1), JOHN WAYNE (4), BETTOR CHEER (9), ROCK HAMMER (3) SUGGESTED BET: NEXT TO ME (1) to win.

SALLY BIGTIME (7) drew poorly last time out and was left without cover there battling on well for third behind Golden Fire and Tremendous Sensation. She draws poorly again this time but finds a much weaker race and should be able to settle close enough and run well from there. LUVARECHS (1) has moderate gate speed and should be able to drive through and hold a prominent position early. She has been unlucky to bump into Golden Fire on a number of occasions this campaign and could be suited finding a race without her this time. ISLA ROCHELLE (2) has a great draw in this race to settle close enough without doing too much work in the early stages. She was an impressive winner rating good time at this track three starts ago running over the top late. DEBBIE LINCOLN (3) returns from a spell in this race having trialled up nicely winning a recent trial. She has high speed and should go well from a low draw where she can settle close in this race. SELECTIONS: SALLY BIGTIME (7), LUVARECHS (1), ISLA ROCHELLE (2), DEBBIE LINCOLN (3) SUGGESTED BET: SALLY BIGTIME (7) to win.

GOLDEN SUNSET (1) should be able to drive through and lead in this race. She was excellent last time out when running over the top to score a nice win. She should run well again in this race. KEAYANG STUKA (5) has recently changed stables and starts first up in this race. He ran fourth two starts ago in the first round of heats of the Inter Dominion after starting one of the favourites in a race taken out by Lovemeto. He looks well placed in this race. PINNIE (2) looks likely to get a very economical run in this race just behind the speed. She sat close to the speed last time out in a race taken out by key rival GOLDEN SUNSET (1) last time out from the stand start. LOVE GUN (3) should get a good run just off the speed in this race. He was forced to race without cover last time out and could be better suited with a softer run. SELECTIONS: GOLDEN SUNSET (1), KEAYANG STUKA (5), PINNIE (2), LOVE GUN (3) SUGGESTED BET: GOLDEN SUNSET (1) to win.

FEAR THE PAIN (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in the early stages of this race. She was left without cover last time out and wasn’t suited by that run in a race taken out by Golden Shooz which was dominated by runners on the pegs. THE LADY DIOR (4) was able to work to the lead two starts ago and rated good time there when finishing second behind Harperville. She should settle close enough in this race from the front row draw and looks to find a suitable race. SO MANY MOMENTS (8) should get a good run through in this race behind a gate speed horse. She ran a good second two starts ago behind Miss Bay King Cole and with a similar effort she should run well again. PRINCESS OF SAVOY (3) was seemingly a touch disappointing on QLD debut finishing sixth after securing a soft run on the pegs. She is likely to have derived benefit from the outing and can run a better race second up. SELECTIONS: FEAR THE PAIN (1), THE LADY DIOR (4), SO MANY MOMENTS (8), PRINCESS OF SAVOY (3) SUGGESTED BET: FEAR THE PAIN (1) to win. OVERVIEW:MISS ADDI (4) brings one of the strongest profiles of the program, with a strong record at this track and distance range, and comes off some first-rate form, including a win here two back when able to lead, with strong placings around that, including at Melton. There’s speed inside here, but the smaller field should allow her to map favourably and produce solid final sectionals, which she’s consistently been doing this time in. MASTER LOUEY (1) looks the main danger from the soft pole draw, with Herbertson aboard and the likelihood he will get his chance along the sprint lane after doing little work, trailing the speed as he’s done recently at this track. It all depends on the tempo and the momentum he gets into the straight as to whether he can run down the top pick. HILTONS SPIRIT (2) deserves respect based on current form, which has seen him win 3 from 10 this season, along with some solid recent sectionals last start at Melton. This is another strong race, but his soft map has him in the mix. KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3) is an interesting runner returning to VIC and his former stable, and did perform well earlier in the year. He has early gate speed and will no doubt look to be on the front end; just prefer to see him against this line-up. WOTDIDUSAAY (6) caused a big upset at Echuca and deserves consideration on that effort; this draw makes things a little tricky, however. BACK: MISS ADDI (4) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:MISS ADDI (4), MASTER LOUEY (1), HILTONS SPIRIT (2), KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3)

OVERVIEW:CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7) has been very honest, being runner-up in 4 of 6 attempts and racing well at this track. He got a good run and bumped into a handy one last time and just couldn’t match those sectionals when 2nd, while his runs prior were good, often from tricky draws. No favours with his marble again, but I fancy this is one of his most winnable opportunities. TOMBEUR (5) creates interest as a first starter off a trial win in slow time recently, and that was his first outing in a year. He’s from one of the state’s best stables, so monitor any strong market support. MEGALODON (8) is a well-named son of the mare Classic Shark and has shown promise in two career outings, finishing 3rd on both occasions. He goes from better draws to the back row but can get an economical peg run here and get his chance late. SIR KITT (1) is a 2yo who struck a very strong bunch of his own age on debut and now takes on more experienced types. He has a soft draw, and these shouldn’t put down the sectionals he faced last time, so he is open to improvement. BACK: CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7), TOMBEUR (5), MEGALODON (8), SIR KITT (1)

OVERVIEW:LIBERTY STAR DUST (5) is racing well, with a good win four back at Kilmore when given an ace drive, then went very close to winning at Geelong two back. Around those efforts, he was racing against the elite of his age group in the Vicbred Series. He’s only had the one start at Cranbourne for a win, and although he’ll need luck from the draw, he is a strong winning hope. CYCLONE JENNI (7) did a really nice job in winning from an awkward draw at this track four back and has been a little out of her depth class-wise since in the Vicbred. The draw is very tricky here but she deserves respect based on what she’s capable of. STORM VENDETTA (1) looks to get a very cosy run from the inside draw and has been racing well in his three runs for the new stable. He meets a few handy ones but must be included in exotics. HEZ HARRYWHO (2) finds a good draw and distance here to buck the trend of form he’s been in. That was the case four back when he found the front over the mile and wasn’t for catching at Kilmore. Look for a big bounce back on those key form indicators. FARROH JOE (3) is a 2yo taking on the older horses here and has run well in similar circumstances before, albeit in slightly easier company. He placed 2nd in his heat and 7th in the final of the Vicbred Series. WEONA OUR RIGHTS (4) is going okay, with his only failure to place this season coming when he drew wide in a Vicbred heat. He’s in the mix with the right run. SELECTIONS:LIBERTY STAR DUST (5), CYCLONE JENNI (7), STORM VENDETTA (1), HEZ HARRYWHO (2)

OVERVIEW: A good-quality race with a mix of 2 and 3yos, with the younger pair of LETITRIDELUV (2) and filly TWIGSTAR (3) looking the standout options. It’s agonising to make a definitive call between two horses who are racing so well at this level, but I must lean to TWIGSTAR (3) based on her excellent debut where she settled back in the field and ran away from them over the short trip. She now has a more favourable draw to press forward over the longer trip and potentially look for the lead. She’s already proven she can run time and, with natural improvement, will be very hard to catch. LETITRIDELUV (2) already has a decent scalp in his career in winning his maiden, then has acquitted himself very well against the elite of his age group in the Vicbred Series. He didn’t draw well in any of those races, and this favourable marble guarantees a positive map and every chance to win again; it’s just whether he’s capable of running times comparable to what the top pick did on debut. Would be surprised if that isn’t the quinella, with much of the remainder having claims at the minor end. BROADWAY OBSESSION (9) may be next best based on a strong SP profile and a solid place strike rate, with SWEET LADY LOU (8) and CALIFORNIA COOL (1) both benefiting from being on the peg line in what should be a strong last half. BACK: TWIGSTAR (3) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:TWIGSTAR (3), LETITRIDELUV (2), BROADWAY OBSESSION (9), SWEET LADY LOU (8)

OVERVIEW: Tricky race, being a standing start over the long distance for trotters and not presenting with the most reliable form under the conditions. EMWALLEN (3) has the most upside, being a lightly raced 5yo, winning 4 from 12 including two solid wins when able to lead all the way recently. This is his first crack under standing-start conditions, which is a slight concern considering some of his rivals love the tapes, but if you’re willing to take the risk, his ability can carry him a long way. MAESTRO (8) ticks a few boxes, being the most reliable and adept under standing-start conditions, a country cup winner under similar conditions and securing the services of Chris Alford. He’s a horse who seems to keep coming under slogging conditions, so he can overcome the back mark here. AVANT GUARD (7) will appreciate facing this sort of quality, having raced better types his past few. He was a winner in similar class four back but under mobile conditions. He’s yet to win from the tapes, but this is his best chance. EL CONQUEROR (5) likes the stand and longer trips and brings a favourable SP profile considering the opposition here. He doesn’t win out of turn, but his manners and the opportunity to get in front of some key rivals hold him in good stead. There’s a host of others worth considering, such as SOVEREIGN TIGER (6), who likes this track and is a last-start winner in easier company, and NEPHEW OF SONOKO (9), who, although he prefers mobile conditions, strikes the easiest race he’s faced in a while. SELECTIONS: EMWALLEN (3), MAESTRO (8), AVANT GUARD (7), EL CONQUEROR (5)

OVERVIEW: JUSTLIKEDAVE (7) was able to lead from this draw two back over the shorter trip and bolted in, winning by 18m and running fast time. He ran 2nd last start when a very short-priced favourite, but the run was still good after over-racing back in the field. His record over anything longer than the sprint journey is a concern, but his best form is hard to ignore. ROBLEN RANGER (2) could be a good roughie here, 2nd up from a break after doing plenty of work fresh. He has good speed to utilise this inside draw and map well. He can give cheek at a price and goes in the Quaddie for sure, no matter the odds. ROBLEN DEMON (5) is his stablemate and has been in good form this preparation, sitting tough and winning here two back. The map may be a little tricky but he can strike with the right run. The back-row runners BONA KHAN (8) and ALTA BAYAMO (9) can be very hard to catch, particularly from back-row draws, but they are worth keeping safe with the extra distance should those at the top end overcook things. BACK: ROBLEN RANGER (2) – 0.5 units (win) 1.5 units (place) SELECTIONS: JUSTLIKEDAVE (7), ROBLEN RANGER (2), ROBLEN DEMON (5), BONA KHAN (8)

OVERVIEW:SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) has the advantage of the concession to use a coveted pole draw and his good gate speed to get a comfortable lead over the short trip. He’s run well in his two runs with recent G1-winning driver Blake Pace aboard, and if he can tap the brakes in the middle section and get a lungful of air for the finish, he will be hard to run down. REASON TO LOVE (8) can catch his cover on the peg line and didn’t have much luck last time from a similar position. He can be an improver from the map and should be included in all multiples. CHASING THE WIND (9) has been popular with punters the past couple with Alford aboard, and having to do no work and come with one run here may suit depending on the tempo. ROCKNROLL RAMBO (10) is threatening to win, placing at his last four starts, but he goes to the back-row draw over the short trip, which hurts his chances. However, the closing sectionals shouldn’t be overly quick for him to make up ground late. DELTA STARZ (5) had a flat tyre last time and can improve based on his win four back, while it’s hard to know what to make of POWERLINC (6), but he is worth throwing in the wider Quaddie should you want to be safe. BACK: SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: SIR CANDY CLOUD (1), REASON TO LOVE (8), CHASING THE WIND (9), ROCKNROLL RAMBO (10)

OVERVIEW: PICKLE IT (5) looks the starting point here in a very even race where map and conditions will play a major part. This horse is a very quick beginner, relishes the mile and has a strong record at the track of 29:4-4-8. He’s probably been run off his legs with the times put down his past few, but those times are unlikely here, so he can hold on with the right tempo. OHHEMJAY CRESCO (1) is a one-batter who will be doing his best to hunt up from the pole, but he proved last start at Wagga that when he can roll along, he’s hard to get past. There are several horses that are map-dependent but are going well enough to include: GOZO MAJOR (4), DOT BALL (6), QUICK CRUNCH (7), FINAL BOW (8) and TOPHUT JOHNY (9). If things worked out, a win by any of them wouldn’t surprise at all. Maybe throw them all in the Quaddie if you want to go wide. SELECTIONS:PICKLE IT (5), OHHEMJAY CRESCO (1), QUICK CRUNCH (7), TOPHUT JOHNY (9)
